items.description: Sec. V-A: 'design domain of size 192×64, resulting in 12,288 pixel-level design variables, illustrated in Fig. 2B', but the Fig. 2B caption shows a 'Full-view' of the beam and says 'only half of the domain is optimized' by symmetry. The text never says outright whether 192×64 is the optimized half-beam or the full beam; the 12,288 count favours the half. Which index of v∈R^{192×64} runs along the span is also left implicit (beam convention: 192 along the span). The figure that would settle this is unavailable.
readings: 192 (span) × 64 (depth) elements is the optimized half-beam; full beam is 384×64 (span:depth 6:1); symmetry cut on a 64-element vertical edge
192×64 is the full beam (3:1) and only a 96×64 half is analysed/optimized (inconsistent with the 12,288-variable count)
192×64 full beam optimized as a whole without symmetry reduction (inconsistent with 'only half of the domain is optimized')

items.description: The Fig. 2B caption only says 'both lower corners are supported', and Sec. V-A defers the setup to Ref. [35]. It is not stated which displacement components are fixed (roller or pin).
readings: Roller: only vertical displacement fixed at the outer bottom corner of the half model (simply supported full beam; classic MBB)
Pin: horizontal and vertical displacement fixed at the outer bottom corner (both lower corners pinned in the full beam, which allows horizontal thrust / arch action)

items.description: The Fig. 2B caption names only the 'lower corners'. It is not stated whether the support acts on the single corner node or on a short strip of nodes along the bottom edge.
readings: single corner node
a few (e.g. 2–4) bottom-edge nodes at the outer corner

items.description: Fig. 2B caption: 'Using symmetry, only half of the domain is optimized.' The text does not give the symmetry boundary condition or say which edge of the 192×64 grid is the cut. It also does not say whether the FE analysis, and so the reported compliance of 246, refers to the half model or to the mirrored full beam.
readings: half model: u_x = 0 on all nodes of the left (mid-span) edge; load at top-left, support at bottom-right
mirror image: symmetry edge on the right, load at top-right, support at bottom-left (same layout mirrored, same compliance)
full 384×64 beam analysed with the mirrored design; compliance is twice the half-model value for the same per-half load

items.description: The Fig. 2B caption says only 'A downward force is applied at the center'. The vertical position at mid-span is shown only in the unavailable figure, and Sec. V-A defers to Ref. [35].
readings: top edge at mid-span (top node of the symmetry edge in the half model; classic MBB)
mid-height of the mid-span section (geometric centre of the beam)
bottom edge at mid-span

items.description: The Fig. 2B caption and Eq. 11 refer only to 'a downward force' / F. They do not say whether it is a single nodal point force or is spread over several nodes or elements.
readings: concentrated force on one node
uniform load over a few (e.g. 2–4) top-edge nodes next to the symmetry line

items.description: No magnitude is given for F (Eq. 11). For the half model it is also unstated whether the full central load or half of it is applied at the symmetry node. Either choice rescales the reported compliance of 246.
readings: F = 1 at the symmetry node of the half model (full-beam load 2)
full-beam load 1, i.e. 0.5 applied on the half model
a dimensional load (e.g. in N); compliance scales with F²

items.entity: volume fraction V0 of the 192×64 optimization
items.description: Sec. V-A leaves V0 symbolic ('predefined volume fraction V0'). The value 0.4 is stated only for generating the training data (Sec. V-B). Sec. VI-E calls 0.5 (96×32) and 0.3 (384×128) 'different' volume constraints, which implies but never states 0.4 for the run behind the 246 result.
readings: V0 = 0.5 (classic MBB default)

items.entity: field the volume constraint is imposed on
items.description: Eq. 11 imposes V(v)=V0 on the physical (filtered) density v. Eq. 12 instead enforces V(ṽ)=V0 on the pre-filter sigmoid field, and the cone filter is applied afterwards; the filter is not exactly volume-preserving near the edges. Sec. V-C also says 'the optimizer enforces the volume constraint strictly instead of the DeepONet'.
readings: mean(ṽ) = V0 on the pre-filter field, then apply the cone filter (Eq. 12)
mean(v) = V0 on the filtered physical density (Eq. 11; standard density-filter TO)

items.entity: Young's modulus of the solid material
items.description: No elastic modulus is given; Sec. V-A defers the FE implementation to Ref. [35].
readings: E0 = 1 (normalized)
a dimensional modulus (e.g. 210 GPa); compliance scales as 1/E0

items.description: Not stated anywhere in the text (deferred to Ref. [35]).
Eq. 11 writes K(v) but never gives the interpolation law (SIMP exponent, any continuation). Sec. V-B mentions only 'density-based topology optimization', and the rest is left to Ref. [35].
readings: modified SIMP E = Emin + v^p (E0 − Emin) with p = 3 fixed
SIMP with p continuation from 1 to 3
p = 1 (no penalization; binarization left to the sigmoid parameterization)
RAMP interpolation

items.description: The stiffness lower bound at v = 0, needed for a non-singular K, is not given.
readings: Emin = 1e-9·E0
Emin = 1e-6·E0
Emin = 1e-3·E0
classic SIMP with a density lower bound of 1e-3 instead of Emin

items.description: Plane stress vs plane strain is not stated (only Eq. 11 KU=F is given). Plane strain changes the effective constitutive matrix (effective ν becomes ν/(1−ν)).
readings: plane stress
plane strain

items.description: The thickness of the 2D beam is not given; it only multiplies the stiffness matrix.
readings: t = 1 (unit thickness)
another thickness t; compliance scales as 1/t

items.description: Sec. V-A gives only '12,288 pixel-level design variables' and says the FE implementation follows Ref. [35]. Element type, the one-element-per-pixel mapping and the physical pixel size are not stated. In 2D, square-element stiffness does not depend on element size, so pixel size matters only through the units of the filter radius.
readings: 192×64 unit-square bilinear 4-node (Q4) elements, one per pixel (193×65 nodes)
higher-order (Q8/Q9) square elements on the same grid
FE mesh finer than the design grid (e.g. 2×2 elements per pixel)

items.description: Sec. V-A: 'cone filter with a radius of 2' applied to ṽ 'as in Ref. [35]'. The radius units (element widths vs physical length), the exact weights and the boundary treatment are not given. Boundary options include truncation with renormalization and reflection across the symmetry edge.
readings: r = 2 element widths, weights max(0, 2 − d) between element centres, renormalized and truncated at all domain edges (88-line-style density filter, rmin = 2)
r = 2 element widths with reflective padding across the symmetry edge (behaves like the full-beam filter)
r = 2 element widths applied as a zero-padded convolution without edge renormalization

items.entity: optimizer, design parameterization and stopping criteria
items.description: The 246 result comes from CMA-ES in the DeepONet latent space, and the baseline from 'L-BFGS-based topology optimization', about 1.6% worse (Sec. VI-B). The text gives no iteration counts, tolerances or L-BFGS settings. It also gives no MBB-specific CMA-ES settings: the photonic values (population 20, 100 iterations, σ0=1000) are never said to apply. Anyone re-running on a standard solver has to choose all of these.
readings: L-BFGS on unconstrained pixel logits through the Eq. 12 volume-preserving sigmoid plus the cone filter (Ref. [35]-style pixel parameterization), run to convergence
OC on densities in [0,1] with a density filter of r = 2, stopping when the max design change is below 0.01
MMA on densities in [0,1] with a density filter of r = 2 and a fixed iteration cap

items.description: The starting design for the reference pixel-based optimization is not stated. Sec. V-B says only that the dataset runs were initialized from eroded copies of previous designs.
readings: uniform density V0 everywhere (zero logits in Eq. 12)
random density field with mean V0
eroded copy of a previously optimized design (Sec. V-B procedure)

items.description: Eq. 11 minimizes U^T K U (= F^T U, the compliance), but the Fig. 2B caption calls the objective 'elastic compliance (elastic potential energy)'. Strain energy is ½U^T K U, so it is unclear whether the reported 246 is the compliance or half of it.
readings: objective = U^T K U = F^T U
objective = ½ U^T K U (strain energy, half the compliance)
